reported.title: Heater stays ON above 22 °C because deadband never turns it off
reported.description: The control logic only calls applyHeater(false) when lastC > HEAT_OFF_C (line 66-69), but the measured violations show D9 was not LOW for 5030 ms starting at 1.79 s in the nominal ramp and 3400 ms from 600 ms in the range test, meaning the heater remained ON while temperature was above 22 °C. The band is implemented as a one-shot threshold check with no state latch, so once ON below 18 °C it is only cleared above 22 °C, and the slow-drift case shows a 360 ms wrong-state interval at 11.54 s consistent with the OFF transition lagging the crossing. The comparison uses the stale lastC sampled every 50 ms (line 55) rather than a fresh reading, adding up to 50 ms of delay but not the multi-second errors measured. D9 was in the wrong state for 5030 ms across 1 interval(s), first at 1.79 s: D9 was not LOW for 5030 ms while required (grace 600 ms).

exposing_checks.behaviour: D9 must follow its stimulus; HIGH when A0 < 18; LOW when A0 > 22; within 600 ms (Heat below 18, off above 22)

judge_input.spec:
- Cabin LM35 on A0 at 10 mV/°C; heater enable on D9; frost override on D2 (pull-up, active LOW).
- Turn the heater ON when temperature is below 18.0 °C and OFF when temperature is above 22.0 °C.
- While D2 is held LOW, force the heater ON regardless of temperature.
- Reach the commanded heater state within 600 ms of a sustained band crossing.
- Print `cabin: <temp> C heat=ON` or `cabin: <temp> C heat=OFF` every 1000 ms with one decimal place.
- Temperature in the status line is informational; control decisions use the comfort band above.

exposing_checks.behaviour: D9 must follow its stimulus; HIGH when A0 < 18; LOW when A0 > 22; within 600 ms (Heat below 18, off above 22)
